issues.description: extract_arch_from_url silently returns None and the caller interpolates it into the URL, producing '.../latest/None/Packages/...'
issues.detail: On regex miss the function returns None and the f-string embeds the literal string 'None' into the koji path. A corrupt URL flows downstream as if valid, surfacing as a 404 far from the cause. Either raise on miss or have the caller refuse to continue.

issues.description: nevra[0] uses the filename's first character rather than the package name's first letter, breaking koji's Packages subdirectory convention
issues.detail: Koji's /Packages/<letter>/ tree is keyed by the lowercased first letter of the package NAME. The code takes the first char of the basename, conflating filename-first-char with name-first-letter. Works by accident today; the invariant is unstated. Parse the name from the NEVRA properly or document and assert the precondition.

issues.description: Arch is read from a regex scan of the whole URL instead of the NEVRA filename, creating two sources of truth that can disagree
issues.detail: Every RPM filename ends in .<arch>.rpm — the canonical value. Regex-scanning the entire URL path can return the first arch token it finds (e.g. /ppc64le-mirror/.../foo.x86_64.rpm), misclassifying the package. Read arch from the NEVRA suffix or thread it from the caller, which already knows it. noarch is also unhandled.

issues.description: Race condition with coreos-koji-tagger is acknowledged in the commit message and shipped with no in-code mitigation or comment
issues.detail: URLs are fabricated before the artifact is tagged into coreos-pool. 'It is safe' is asserted, not reasoned — no retry, no detection, no module docstring naming the temporal invariant. Future maintainers debugging a 404 will not find this in the code. Add a comment stating the precondition that the lockfile is consumed only after tagging completes.

issues.description: Hardcoded arch list and koji base URL belong at module scope as a single source of truth
issues.detail: The arch list inside extract_arch_from_url is independent of the arches generate_main iterates over, and the koji base URL is a string literal embedded in logic. A change to either silently drifts from the other. Lift both to module-level constants so the supported-arch set and koji layout are inspectable in one place.

issues.description: No unit tests for the new pure functions, and the prioritize-coreos-pool branch in query_packages_location is now likely vestigial
issues.detail: use_koji_url_only and extract_arch_from_url are pure, deterministic, and trivially testable — a handful of representative URLs would have caught the nevra[0] and None-arch defects. Separately, the older prioritization branch now duplicates work the rewriter does downstream; either delete it or comment why it remains load-bearing.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on NEEDS-WORK. Two defects are unanimous or near-unanimous: extract_arch_from_url silently returns None and the caller embeds the literal string 'None' into the koji path, and nevra[0] takes the filename's first character rather than the package name's first letter. The arch is read from a whole-URL regex scan instead of the NEVRA filename, creating a second source of truth that can disagree and ignoring noarch. The race with coreos-koji-tagger is acknowledged in the commit message but shipped with no in-code mitigation, comment, or stated invariant. Lift the arch list and koji base URL to module-level constants, add unit tests for the new pure functions, and decide whether the legacy prioritize-coreos-pool branch in query_packages_location is now dead code.
